title: Surgical unconsciousness with preserved breathing and circulatory control

concept.text: The proposed innovation is an anesthetic method that reliably produces unconsciousness suitable for surgery while largely preserving spontaneous breathing, airway protection and cardiovascular control. It would need to maintain these functions at clinically useful doses, throughout anesthesia and during painful surgical stimulation. Its defining achievement would be the combination of dependable unconsciousness, adequate surgical conditions and substantially reduced physiological disruption.

Conceptual synthesis. Each component requires separate assessment. Spontaneous breathing describes continued respiratory activity. Adequate ventilation requires sufficient gas exchange, while airway protection concerns the ability to keep harmful material out of the lungs. Analgesia, surgical immobility and cardiovascular stability add further requirements. Demonstrating any one of these functions would establish only part of the proposed capability.

significance.text: The clinical motivation is substantial. The supplied ciprofol study describes apnea and cardiovascular depression among propofol's recognized adverse effects and documents the need for anesthetics that retain desirable effects while reducing adverse events. Its use of rescue medication for hypotension illustrates the physiological support that can accompany anesthetic induction.

Conditional impact synthesis. Dependable surgical unconsciousness with preserved respiratory and circulatory function could substantially reduce clinically important interventions and dependence on physiological support. The potential advance would be greatest if it extended across demanding operations and patients particularly vulnerable to respiratory or hemodynamic instability. Such breadth would change the practical physiological burden of anesthesia.

Conditional downstream synthesis. Reduced support requirements could make some operations more feasible where advanced physiological support is difficult to provide. Deployment would still depend on monitoring, rescue capacity, trained personnel and procedure-specific validation. The operation's own risks would persist, and some procedures would continue to require airway instrumentation, assisted ventilation or muscle relaxation. Benefits in access, complications and recovery would each require direct evidence.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target capability is to separate dependable surgical unconsciousness from unwanted depression of respiratory and cardiovascular control at clinically useful doses and during noxious stimulation. The supplied source supports the clinical motivation through its discussion of apnea and cardiovascular depression. Field-wide availability of the broader capability as of November 1, 2026 remains unresolved in the supplied evidence.

Scientific and engineering synthesis. The central barrier is achieving the desired brain state while retaining the physiological functions needed for safe surgery. A method must sustain unconsciousness through changing surgical stimulation while preserving sufficient ventilation, airway protection and circulatory stability. It must also provide compatible analgesia and immobility, either intrinsically or through adjuncts whose effects are included in the assessment. Complete separation remains an open biological question.

Possible research approaches include new molecular targets, combinations of agents and targeted delivery. These are hypotheses supplied with the concept. Their feasibility and ability to deliver the full capability remain unestablished by the cited study. A concrete development challenge is to show that any physiological advantage persists across doses, patients, adjunct medications and surgical conditions, with rescue treatment accounted for explicitly.

current_state.text: Qianmei Zhu, Zhen Luo and colleagues published a multicenter phase 2a comparison of ciprofol and propofol online on January 21, 2023. The trial ran from December 2016 to July 2018 at seven centers. It enrolled 109 selected elective-surgery patients aged 18–65 with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I–II. The study used an open-label, nonrandomized, active-controlled design, and eligibility required tracheal intubation. These characteristics limit its applicability to high-risk patients and to the broader proposed capability.

The study reported successful induction in all patients, with no patient receiving more than one top-up dose. According to the supplied review, the main results and Table 1 show that two patients needed a top-up, qualifying the abstract's broader wording about initial-bolus success. The investigators reported no statistically significant differences in total adverse-event incidence or severity between the investigated groups. Safety equivalence remains unestablished by these nonsignificant comparisons.

Patients also received midazolam, sufentanil and rocuronium, and maintenance anesthesia was unprotocolized. The authors attributed comparable hemodynamic stability during induction to prompt rescue treatment. Reported hypotension treatments included intravenous ephedrine 3 mg, metaraminol 0.3 mg or methoxamine 1 mg. These details prevent attribution of observed stability solely to preservation of intrinsic circulatory control. Preserved protective airway reflexes and spontaneous ventilation throughout major surgery remain unestablished by this induction study.

The supplied review reports verified article identity and complete extracted text for all ten main-article pages through the references, without truncation. Referenced supplements and figure images were unavailable to that review. The historical findings above therefore rely on the reviewed main-article text. The supplied record contains no freshness search establishing subsequent progress through November 1, 2026, so present-day field-wide availability remains an open evidence question. This coverage limitation leaves the historical induction findings intact.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration. Multicenter comparative trials would show dependable unconsciousness and adequate surgical conditions across major operations and high-risk populations, together with prespecified, clinically meaningful reductions in respiratory and hemodynamic interventions relative to current best practice. The protocol would define improvement thresholds in advance. These are proposed operational criteria whose clinical justification would need to be established for the intended uses.
completion_criteria.label: Trials demonstrate surgical unconsciousness with prespecified reductions in interventions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed functional assessment. Studies would directly measure airway protection, spontaneous ventilation and cardiovascular stability throughout anesthesia and noxious stimulation. They would separately assess awareness, analgesia, immobility, aspiration, oxygenation, ventilation, organ injury and recovery. Recording adjunct medications, rescue treatments and intervention thresholds would help determine how much physiological stability the method itself preserves. Intervention counts would be interpreted alongside these direct measurements because treatment practices can influence the counts.
completion_criteria.label: Measure airway protection, spontaneous ventilation and cardiovascular stability

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries. Independent teams would reproduce the findings across centers, patient groups and relevant procedures using transparent dosing and rescue protocols. Reports would identify failures, contraindications and operations that continue to require airway support, assisted ventilation or muscle relaxation. Evaluation in resource-constrained settings would assess the monitoring and rescue capacity needed for safe deployment. A finite trial program would establish demonstrated breadth within its tested conditions, with further evidence needed for additional populations and procedures.
completion_criteria.label: Independent teams reproduce findings and report practical deployment limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based conceptual synthesis. ANS-01, A causal theory of anesthetic-induced unconsciousness, could help identify mechanisms that permit unconsciousness with less physiological disruption. ANS-04 concerns achieving that clinical capability, while ANS-01 concerns explaining its underlying causes. ANS-02, A reliable real-time monitor of conscious experience during anesthesia, could support assessment of dependable unconsciousness and awareness risk. Respiratory and cardiovascular preservation would still require their own measurements.

Roster-based conceptual synthesis. ANS-03, A broadly applicable, pain-selective surgical nerve block, and ANS-07, Systemic, non-opioid analgesia for severe perioperative pain, overlap with ANS-04 through control of surgical pain and the effects of adjunct drugs. Their respective targets are regional pain-selective blockade and systemic analgesia. ANS-04 targets surgical unconsciousness with physiological preservation. Effective analgesia could contribute to the combined method, with unconsciousness, ventilation and airway protection assessed separately.

Roster-based conceptual synthesis. ANS-05, A radically accessible, resilient anesthesia platform for essential surgery, shares the possibility of making anesthesia feasible in difficult settings. Its platform-level scope also encompasses delivery and operational resilience. ANS-08, Reliable rescue oxygenation in the difficult airway, addresses rescue when oxygenation is threatened. ANS-04 seeks to reduce physiological disruption during anesthesia, with procedure-specific rescue requirements remaining part of practical validation.

Roster-based conceptual synthesis. ANS-06, Broad, active reversal of general anesthesia, concerns reliably ending anesthetic effects. ANS-04 concerns maintaining a suitable anesthetic state while preserving breathing and circulatory control. A method could perform well on either capability independently, so reversal and physiological preservation need distinct demonstrations.

Roster-based conceptual synthesis. ANS-09, Mechanism-based prevention of chronic postsurgical pain, and ANS-10, Mechanism-guided anesthesia to prevent postoperative brain dysfunction, concern longer-term pain and postoperative brain outcomes. ANS-04 focuses on physiological preservation during surgical unconsciousness. Better intraoperative physiology could plausibly influence later outcomes, but benefits for chronic pain or brain dysfunction would require dedicated evidence.

unresolved_issues: The supplied material does not establish field-wide availability of the full capability as of November 1, 2026.
The biological feasibility and practical degree of separating surgical unconsciousness from respiratory and cardiovascular depression remain open.
The supplied study does not evaluate whether new targets, combinations or targeted delivery can deliver the proposed capability.
Protective airway reflexes, sustained spontaneous ventilation and intrinsic circulatory control throughout major surgery remain unestablished by the cited induction trial.
The abstract and main results differ in their characterization of initial-bolus success. This record follows the main-results account identified in the supplied review.
Referenced supplements and figure images were unavailable to the supplied review, leaving their contents unassessed.
Clinically meaningful improvement thresholds, sufficient reproducibility and the breadth of procedures and patient groups required for adoption remain to be specified and justified.
Expanded access and improved longer-term outcomes remain conditional possibilities requiring dedicated validation.

brief.title: Surgery with natural breathing and steady blood pressure
possible: You could remain reliably unconscious during surgery while breathing on your own, keeping harmful material out of your lungs and maintaining stable blood pressure. The method would also need to allow pain control and keep you still throughout the operation.
why: Patients could need fewer interventions to support breathing and blood pressure during anesthesia, the drugs used to keep them unconscious for surgery. This would especially matter for people vulnerable to breathing or circulatory problems.
Lower support needs could make some operations more feasible in places where advanced equipment and physiological support are difficult to provide.

sources.who: Qianmei Zhu, Zhen Luo and colleagues
sources.showed: Ciprofol and propofol both successfully started anesthesia in selected surgical patients. The nonrandomized trial found no statistically significant difference in unwanted effects.
sources.quote: There were no significant differences in the incidences and severity of AEs in the dose ranges investigated of ciprofol vs. propofol.
sources.cited_for: Ciprofol can start anesthesia, but this trial does not establish a safety advantage over propofol.
sources.not_established: Patients received breathing tubes and other drugs; preserved breathing, airway protection and unaided blood pressure control remain unproven.

sources.who: Xin Zhang, Hui-Xian Li and colleagues
sources.showed: In a randomized trial at one center, remimazolam caused fewer episodes of low blood oxygen and low blood pressure than propofol during a short cervical operation without breathing tubes. Awakening took longer.
sources.quote: Compared with patients in the P group, patients in the R group had fewer changes in the respiratory rate, mean arterial pressure and heart rate at some time points during surgery.
sources.cited_for: Remimazolam reduced breathing and blood pressure problems during a short operation.
sources.not_established: Low blood oxygen remained common; the trial did not establish airway protection or preserved function across major operations and high-risk patients.

sources.showed: In a randomized trial in older surgical patients, remimazolam caused fewer episodes of low blood pressure than propofol. Recovery outcomes were comparable.
sources.quote: Secondary outcomes such as recovery time, delirium, and postoperative nausea and vomiting were comparable in both groups.
sources.cited_for: Remimazolam reduced low blood pressure during surgery in older patients.
sources.not_established: Patients received breathing tubes and muscle-relaxing drugs, so the trial did not demonstrate preserved spontaneous breathing or airway protection.

shown: Xin Zhang and colleagues demonstrated part of the goal during a short cervical operation: patients breathed on their own with remimazolam and had fewer oxygen and blood pressure problems than with propofol. The trial involved 90 patients at one center, and low oxygen remained common.

Yeong-Gwan Jeon and colleagues found fewer blood pressure drops with remimazolam in older surgical patients, but used breathing tubes and muscle-relaxing drugs. Neither trial demonstrated the full combination of reliable unconsciousness, protected lungs and preserved breathing and circulation.
missing: No method has demonstrated the full combination throughout major surgery, including during painful stimulation.
Direct tests must establish adequate gas exchange and protection against harmful material entering the lungs, alongside unconsciousness and stillness.
Benefits must persist across doses, other drugs and vulnerable patients, with rescue treatments accounted for.
Independent teams must establish where the method works and what monitoring and rescue support it requires.

milestones.label: Trials demonstrate unconsciousness with fewer support interventions
milestones.explanation: Trials across centers would have to show reliable unconsciousness and suitable surgical conditions with predefined reductions in breathing and blood pressure interventions. Major operations and high-risk patients would test its breadth.

milestones.label: Measurements confirm breathing, airway protection and stable circulation
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to measure these functions throughout anesthesia and painful stimulation, alongside awareness, pain control, movement, injury and recovery. Tracking other drugs and rescue treatments would clarify the method's contribution.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce results and establish practical limits
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce results across patients and procedures, reporting failures and support needs, including in settings with limited resources. This would establish the conditions in which the method works.

uncertain: How far can surgical unconsciousness be separated biologically from suppression of breathing and circulation?
What reduction in support interventions would count as a meaningful clinical improvement?
How much replication, across which operations and patient groups, would justify adoption?

page.title: General anaesthesia with preserved cardiorespiratory function
page.definition: A general anaesthetic regimen would keep patients unarousable even to painful stimulation during surgery. From induction through the end of surgery, patients would breathe sufficiently to take up oxygen and clear carbon dioxide, keep their airway open, protect their lungs against aspiration and maintain circulation without rescue. These properties apply to the full drug combination. Ketamine can preserve throat reflexes during anaesthesia, yet vomiting and aspiration can still occur.

goal.need: In 95,407 general anaesthetics for noncardiac surgery at two hospitals, 6.8% of patients had oxygen saturation below 90% for at least two minutes between induction and emergence. Lighter sedation can leave patients responsive to pain. For operations requiring unconsciousness, preserving breathing and circulation could spare patients assisted breaths or drugs to raise blood pressure when the anaesthetic itself would otherwise make them necessary. Patients would still need monitoring throughout anaesthesia.

completion.title: Surgical general anaesthesia preserves gas exchange, airway protection and circulation throughout surgery.
completion.criterion: A prospective, peer-reviewed surgical study shows that the full regimen induces unarousability to painful stimulation and maintains it throughout surgery. From the start of induction to the end of surgery, assess spontaneous oxygenation and carbon-dioxide clearance, airway patency, protection against aspiration, and cardiovascular function in the same patients. Assisted ventilation, airway rescue and vasoactive rescue count as failures. Assess the patient's own airway protection directly and record clinical aspiration outcomes. An airway device that supplies protection cannot establish this component. The claim is limited to the operation, population and doses studied.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback. ASA defines general anaesthetic depth. No external body was identified that sets the joint surgical test.
completion.basis: ASA defines general anaesthetic depth by unarousability to painful stimulation. NIH identifies stable physiological functions as a drug-development goal. Ketamine labelling distinguishes active throat reflexes from protection against aspiration. Radiographic studies have assessed aspiration directly after induction. No external whole-operation threshold, acceptable failure rate or required sample size was identified.

milestones.title: A candidate anaesthetic prevents a mouse from righting itself within 30 seconds.
milestones.criterion: During anaesthetic infusion, place the mouse on its back. Score loss of the righting reflex if it fails to return to all four paws within 30 seconds. This is a behavioural measure of hypnotic activity.
milestones.set_by: Anaesthesia research convention of loss of righting reflex, using the 30-second implementation published by Zhou et al., section 4.5.
milestones.threshold_quote: If a mouse failed to turn over onto its four paws within 30 s, it was in a state of LORR.

milestones.title: An initial anaesthetic bolus produces a MOAA/S score ≤1 at two minutes.
milestones.criterion: In surgical patients aged 18–65 years given midazolam and sufentanil before the study hypnotic, assess the Modified Observer’s Assessment of Alertness/Sedation score two minutes after the initial bolus starts. Report the proportion scoring ≤1 before any top-up dose.
milestones.set_by: Zhu et al., published protocol and results of phase 2a study NCT03698617, retrospectively registered. The endpoint concerns induction.
milestones.threshold_quote: The success of induction was defined as a MOAA/S score ≤ 1, 2 min after the start of ciprofol or propofol administration.

milestones.title: A surgical anaesthetic prevents awakening, recall, rescue sedation and movement throughout surgery.
milestones.criterion: Score the surgical anaesthetic as effective for a patient only if all three conditions hold during general anaesthesia: no intraoperative awakening or recall, no need for a rescue sedative, and no body movement.
milestones.set_by: Doi et al., combined primary efficacy endpoint of registered phase IIb/III study JapicCTI-121973.
milestones.threshold_quote: no intraoperative awakening/recall, no need for rescue sedatives, and no body movements.

milestones.title: Fewer patients aged 65–80 develop systolic pressure <90 mmHg on remimazolam than on propofol.
milestones.criterion: In patients aged 65–80 undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy or transurethral resection of a bladder tumour, compare remimazolam with propofol during general anaesthesia with remifentanil, rocuronium and tracheal intubation. The proportion of patients with any systolic blood pressure <90 mmHg must be lower with remimazolam at P<0.05.
milestones.set_by: Jeon et al., primary outcome and statistical criterion of registered study KCT0006719. The protocol concerns patients aged 65–80 years undergoing the two specified operations.
milestones.threshold_quote: Hypotension was defined as systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg.

milestones.title: Fewer conization patients reach oxygen saturation ≤95% on remimazolam than on propofol.
milestones.criterion: During cold-knife conization with spontaneous breathing and face-mask oxygen, compare remimazolam with propofol, each with fentanyl and an electroencephalographic Patient State Index of 35–50. Count patients whose peripheral oxygen saturation falls to ≤95% with no increasing trend. The proportion must be lower with remimazolam at P<0.05. The protocol permits rescue mask ventilation.
milestones.set_by: Zhang et al., primary outcome and statistical criterion of registered study ChiCTR2200065519. The protocol concerns cold-knife conization.
milestones.threshold_quote: 95 or lower with no increasing trend.

milestones.title: A surgical regimen sustains unresponsiveness, spontaneous gas exchange and circulation without rescue.
milestones.criterion: In a prospective surgical study, the complete regimen induces unarousability to painful stimulation and maintains it throughout surgery. In the same patients, spontaneous oxygenation, carbon-dioxide clearance and cardiovascular function remain adequate from the start of induction through the end of surgery. Assisted ventilation, airway rescue or vasoactive rescue counts as failure.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback. No external test was identified that requires surgical unarousability, unsupported gas exchange and preserved circulation through the end of the operation.

milestones.title: More patients meet the 15-minute depth and cardiorespiratory endpoint on ciprofol than on propofol.
milestones.criterion: In elective surgery, show superiority to propofol (two-sided P<0.05). Induction requires MOAA/S ≤1, at most one top-up and no rescue hypnotic. Until 15 min from dosing or an earlier second intubation attempt, require no signs of inadequate depth, extra rocuronium for intubation, or two consecutive stimulus-related rises >20% in systolic, diastolic or mean pressure. Allow at most one bispectral index reading >60 after its nadir. Before rocuronium, exclude apnoea or saturation <90% lasting >30 s, or respiratory depression needing immediate intervention. Exclude systolic pressure <90 mmHg for >2 min requiring treatment, or life-threatening hypotension needing immediate intervention.
milestones.set_by: Haisco-USA, registered study NCT04711837 (HSK3486-304), statistical analysis plan sections 3.2 and 7.6.2.
milestones.threshold_quote: provides better anesthetic effects compared to propofol 2.0/1.0 mg/kg without significant cardiac and respiratory depression

not_found: No external joint completion threshold, acceptable failure rate or required sample size was located for the full capability.
No study located in the searches demonstrated the complete capability with direct assessment of protection against aspiration throughout surgery.
The full text of Doi et al. was paywalled, and its endpoint and efficacy result were available in the publisher’s abstract.
No registered trial or professional standard was identified that jointly requires surgical unarousability, unsupported gas exchange and preserved circulation through the end of surgery.
No regulator or professional society statement was located that disputes the value or feasibility of the combined goal.

results.finding: Among 30 thoracoscopic surgery patients receiving tubeless anaesthesia with intended spontaneous ventilation, 100% developed intraoperative hypercapnia.
results.detail: The tubeless arm used a planned laryngeal mask with supplemental oxygen. The protocol permitted assisted ventilation and conversion to intubation. The paper reports vasoactive drug use for blood-pressure control but gives no patient-level rescue counts.

definition = "A general anaesthetic regimen would keep patients unarousable even to painful stimulation during surgery. From induction through the end of surgery, patients would breathe sufficiently to take up oxygen and clear carbon dioxide, keep their airway open, protect their lungs against aspiration and maintain circulation without rescue. These properties apply to the full drug combination. Ketamine can preserve throat reflexes during anaesthesia, yet vomiting and aspiration can still occur.". Reason: The definition gains a clinical comparator and explains why retained throat reflexes alone cannot establish protection against aspiration.

goal.need = "In 95,407 general anaesthetics for noncardiac surgery at two hospitals, 6.8% of patients had oxygen saturation below 90% for at least two minutes between induction and emergence. Lighter sedation can leave patients responsive to pain. For operations requiring unconsciousness, preserving breathing and circulation could spare patients assisted breaths or drugs to raise blood pressure when the anaesthetic itself would otherwise make them necessary. Patients would still need monitoring throughout anaesthesia.". Reason: The two-hospital estimate gives the frequency and duration of low oxygen saturation, and the clinical trial identifies the rescue treatments patients could avoid.

add statement by U.S. Army, Borden Institute, Anesthesia and Perioperative Care of the Combat Casualty, 1995: "preservation of airway reflexes with minimal hemodynamic effects". Reason: The Army textbook explicitly identifies airway-reflex preservation and minimal circulatory effects as desirable properties of anaesthesia for combat casualties.

edit completion: criterion = "A prospective, peer-reviewed surgical study shows that the full regimen induces unarousability to painful stimulation and maintains it throughout surgery. From the start of induction to the end of surgery, assess spontaneous oxygenation and carbon-dioxide clearance, airway patency, protection against aspiration, and cardiovascular function in the same patients. Assisted ventilation, airway rescue and vasoactive rescue count as failures. Assess the patient's own airway protection directly and record clinical aspiration outcomes. An airway device that supplies protection cannot establish this component. The claim is limited to the operation, population and doses studied."; set_by = "Atlas fallback. ASA defines general anaesthetic depth. No external body was identified that sets the joint surgical test."; basis = "ASA defines general anaesthetic depth by unarousability to painful stimulation. NIH identifies stable physiological functions as a drug-development goal. Ketamine labelling distinguishes active throat reflexes from protection against aspiration. Radiographic studies have assessed aspiration directly after induction. No external whole-operation threshold, acceptable failure rate or required sample size was identified."; refs = [2, 3, 4, 13]. Reason: The criterion distinguishes achieving unconsciousness during induction from maintaining it during surgery and accounts for a planned airway device that itself provides protection.

edit m1: criterion = "During anaesthetic infusion, place the mouse on its back. Score loss of the righting reflex if it fails to return to all four paws within 30 seconds. This is a behavioural measure of hypnotic activity.". Reason: The mouse assay needs its behavioural threshold in the criterion, while the cohort size and ciprofol findings belong with the result.

edit m2: title = "An initial anaesthetic bolus produces a MOAA/S score \u22641 at two minutes."; criterion = "In surgical patients aged 18\u201365 years given midazolam and sufentanil before the study hypnotic, assess the Modified Observer\u2019s Assessment of Alertness/Sedation score two minutes after the initial bolus starts. Report the proportion scoring \u22641 before any top-up dose."; threshold_quote = "The success of induction was defined as a MOAA/S score\u2009\u2264\u20091, 2\u00a0min after the start of ciprofol or propofol administration."; threshold_ref = 6. Reason: The protocol scores initial-bolus success at the two-minute assessment and reports the proportion of patients who qualify before a top-up.

add milestone after m2: "More patients meet the 15-minute depth and cardiorespiratory endpoint on ciprofol than on propofol.". Reason: HSK3486-304 specifies a joint induction endpoint between a sedation score alone and unsupported function throughout surgery.

edit m3: criterion = "Score the surgical anaesthetic as effective for a patient only if all three conditions hold during general anaesthesia: no intraoperative awakening or recall, no need for a rescue sedative, and no body movement.". Reason: The three-part efficacy endpoint can be stated without the trial's enrolment, success rate or recovery outcome.

edit m4: title = "Fewer patients aged 65\u201380 develop systolic pressure <90 mmHg on remimazolam than on propofol."; criterion = "In patients aged 65\u201380 undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy or transurethral resection of a bladder tumour, compare remimazolam with propofol during general anaesthesia with remifentanil, rocuronium and tracheal intubation. The proportion of patients with any systolic blood pressure <90 mmHg must be lower with remimazolam at P<0.05.". Reason: The primary outcome counts patients who develop hypotension, whereas the title could be read as counting repeated episodes in each patient.

edit m5: title = "Fewer conization patients reach oxygen saturation \u226495% on remimazolam than on propofol."; criterion = "During cold-knife conization with spontaneous breathing and face-mask oxygen, compare remimazolam with propofol, each with fentanyl and an electroencephalographic Patient State Index of 35\u201350. Count patients whose peripheral oxygen saturation falls to \u226495% with no increasing trend. The proportion must be lower with remimazolam at P<0.05. The protocol permits rescue mask ventilation.". Reason: The conization endpoint counts patients meeting a specified saturation threshold under supplemental oxygen, with mask ventilation available for rescue.

edit m6: criterion = "In a prospective surgical study, the complete regimen induces unarousability to painful stimulation and maintains it throughout surgery. In the same patients, spontaneous oxygenation, carbon-dioxide clearance and cardiovascular function remain adequate from the start of induction through the end of surgery. Assisted ventilation, airway rescue or vasoactive rescue counts as failure."; set_by = "Atlas fallback. No external test was identified that requires surgical unarousability, unsupported gas exchange and preserved circulation through the end of the operation."; refs = [1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 14]. Reason: The whole-operation milestone needs to distinguish the onset of unconsciousness from the start of physiological assessment and from the published induction-only composite.

add not found: "No regulator or professional society statement was located that disputes the value or feasibility of the combined goal.". Reason: A drug-specific aspiration warning cannot establish professional opposition to the broader goal.
remove statement 2. Reason: The KETALAR label warns that aspiration can occur despite active reflexes and makes no recommendation to develop the proposed regimen.
